Final for Publication

Application # 23005-T1

17-13-0303-C(1) Substitute Type 1 Narrative & Plans ~ 1040 West Belmont Avenue, Chicago,
IL

Proposed Zoning: B3-5 Community Shopping District
Lot Area: 8,250 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to develop the subject property with a new five-
story mixed-use building containing approximately 4,425 sq. ft. of retail
space at grade and twenty-eight (28) dwelling units above. The proposed
building will measure 68 ft.-10 in. in height. The subject property is a
Transit Served Location and will be supported by six (6) off-street parking
spaces and twenty-eight (28) onsite bicycle parking spaces. Pursuant to Sec.
17-13-0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and Variation and
pursuant to Secs. 17-13-1003-EE, 17-13-1101-B, and 17-13-1101-D of the
Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the
residential off-street parking ratio from 50% (14 parking spaces) to 21.4%
(6 parking spaces), reduce the rear setback for floors containing residential
units from 30 ft. to 15 ft., waive the loading berth requirement, and is
seeking all zoning relief, as needed and as allowed by the Chicago Zoning
Code, for the attached plans.

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 34,719 square feet (4.23 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 294.64 square feet
per D.U. (28 dwelling units)

(C) The amount of off-street parking: 6 parking spaces

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to the CTA Brown Line Belmont Station, Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-
EE, the Applicant is seeking to decrease the off-street parking ratio from 50% (14
parking spaces) to 21.4% (6 parking spaces).

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback: zero
b. Side Setbacks:
West Side: zero
East Side: zero
c. Rear Setback: 15 feet

*Pursuant to Sec, 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential units from 30 feet to 15 feet.

(E) Building Height: 68 feet-10 inches

Final for Publication

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 635 linear feet of the Belmont Avenue CTA
Brown Line Rail Station. The proposed mixed-use building containing retail space at grade
and twenty-eight (28) residential units above will be supported by six (6) off-street parking
spaces and twenty-eight bicycle parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the
Applicant is seeking to reduce the residential off-street parking ratio from 50% (14 parking
spaces) to 21.6% (6 parking spaces).

2, The Applicant’s building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504 because the retail portion and residential entrance of
the proposed building front along West Belmont Avenue and the proposed front setback is
zero. Furthermore, the entrance widths do not exceed 12 ft., the entrance depths do not
exceed the entrance width, the entrances are not more than two-stories in height, and the
proposed building elevations comply with the window transparency requirements.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Belmont Avenue CTA Brown Line Rail Station. The Applicant believes
the development will improve the subject area for residents and other commuters traveling
in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain grade-level retail space and twenty-eight
(28) residential units above. The proposed building will be supported by six (6) off-street
parking spaces and twenty-eight (28) onsite bicycle parking spaces. The Applicant is
seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking ratio reduction (6 parking
spaces proposed) for the residential units pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace a one-story
restaurant building with a new mixed-use building offering new retail spaces along West
Belmont Avenue. The proposed residential units will provide additional residential
housing inventory to meet market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to
mass transit, the Applicant believes the project provides transit options and otherwise
complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules promulgated by the
Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.
